Clases de inglés individuales y grupales. 🚀 Formación interna y oportunidad de especializarte en Blockchain y nuevas tecnologías. 🤝 Un ambiente cercano, una organización horizontal y procesos de decisión ágiles, donde tus ideas y propuestas tendrán un impacto real. 💡 ¿Te apetece afrontar un nuevo reto tecnológico? review_candidates.description: Laboratory System Solutions and Support Engineer The Opportunity We’re looking for an experienced Laboratory Systems & Instrument Integration Engineer to support and develop the technology that connects pharmaceutical laboratory instruments with wider laboratory and informatics systems. The role has a strong hands-on element. You’ll be responsible for understanding how instruments connect, communicate and transfer data into platforms such as LIMS, ELN and SDMS, while troubleshooting issues across instruments, workstations, networks, middleware and laboratory applications. This would suit someone who genuinely understands both sides of the laboratory environment: the scientific instrumentation itself and the IT/infrastructure behind it. What You’ll Be Doing Support the installation, configuration, integration, qualification, troubleshooting and lifecycle management of laboratory instruments. Work across analytical technologies including HPLC, UPLC, GC, LC-MS/MS, GC-MS, spectroscopy, balances, pH meters, titrators and other laboratory equipment. Design and support connectivity between instruments, workstations, laboratory networks, servers and enterprise applications. Troubleshoot instrument connectivity using technologies including Ethernet, TCP/IP, USB, RS-232/RS-485, drivers, middleware and vendor integration tools. Support integrations between laboratory equipment and LIMS, ELN, SDMS and CDS platforms. Investigate failed data transfers, instrument communication issues, application connectivity problems and inaccessible or corrupted files. Provide specialist technical support to laboratory and scientific users. Work closely with QC, analytical teams, IT, automation, infrastructure, cybersecurity, Quality and CSV/CSA teams. Coordinate with instrument manufacturers and software vendors to resolve complex technical issues. Support instrument installations, upgrades, moves, replacements and decommissioning. Contribute to requirements, risk assessments, testing, qualification, validation, SOPs and technical documentation. Ensure laboratory data remains reliable, secure, traceable and compliant throughout the instrument and system lifecycle. What We’re Looking For Hands-on experience supporting laboratory instruments and associated software. Strong understanding of instrument connectivity, integration and troubleshooting. Experience working with laboratory informatics platforms such as LIMS, ELN, SDMS and/or CDS. Experience supporting analytical instrumentation such as HPLC, UPLC, GC, Mass Spectrometry or spectroscopy. Knowledge of laboratory networks, instrument workstations, data acquisition and data-transfer processes. Understanding of connectivity technologies such as TCP/IP, Ethernet, serial communication, drivers and middleware. Strong fault-finding capability across hardware, software, networking and laboratory applications. Experience working within a pharmaceutical or other regulated laboratory environment. Knowledge of GxP, CSV/CSA and laboratory data integrity. Familiarity with regulatory expectations including 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP Annex 11 and ALCOA+. Ability to work effectively across scientific, IT, Quality and vendor teams. Location & Travel The role requires someone who can work from laboratory sites in Kent and collaborate closely with local teams. Travel to pharmaceutical laboratory sites in Ireland and Italy will also be required, including the ability to travel at relatively short notice when necessary. Candidates will therefore need the appropriate passport and work/travel authorisation to undertake the required business travel without avoidable administrative delays. Why This Role? This is a particularly interesting opportunity for someone who doesn’t sit neatly in either traditional IT or laboratory science. You’ll be working across the complete laboratory technology environment, helping ensure analytical instruments are connected correctly, scientific data flows reliably into laboratory applications, and the entire ecosystem continues to operate securely and compliantly. For someone coming from Lab IT, Scientific Systems, Laboratory Informatics, Instrument Integration or Laboratory Systems Support, it offers a broad technical remit covering both hands-on troubleshooting and more complex integration work.

Now, we’re bringing Spatial AI into the sky through high-performance UAVs that can perceive, localize, coordinate, and act in the real world. This requires more than strong algorithms and good hardware. It requires systems that can be configured, calibrated, tested, deployed, demonstrated, debugged, and improved under real field conditions. We’re looking for a hands-on engineer who wants to work close to the product, close to the field, and close to the full autonomy stack. Someone who is not limited to one layer, but follows the problem wherever it leads. You will bring together UAVs, payloads, sensors, onboard compute, autonomy software, operator tools, and partner environments into systems that are ready to fly, test, demonstrate, and deploy. This is a highly hands-on, end-to-end prototyping and field engineering role. You will work directly with other startups, prime contractors, and military institutions, translating their requirements into practical mechanical and electrical designs building on our existing technology. When something is not working, you go where the evidence leads: recalibrate a sensor, debug a radio link, inspect a wiring harness, analyse a flight log, fix a configuration issue, improve a checklist, or bring the right evidence back to the software development team. The problems you will work on are complex, dynamic, and multivariable. You will often have partial information, limited time, and a system where hardware, software, environment, and operator behavior interact in non-obvious ways. Your job is to create clarity, choose the right debugging path, and drive the system toward a robust long-term solution. You will not just operate systems. You will make them better. What You’ll Work On Own the integration project: Consult with partners, clarify requirements, agree interfaces and test criteria, and drive technical decisions and milestones to a working joint system. Cross-Stack Engineering: Design integration concepts, CAD models, electrical circuits and system integration and bring together sensors, enclosures, calibration, compute, mechanisms, power electronics, controls, networking, autonomy software, and operator workflows. Validation & Fieldability Ownership: Put your system through its paces: on test stands and in the field. Spot design flaws, integration gaps, recurring failure modes, and process bottlenecks. And establish confidence in mission-readiness as the maturity is realized. Create clarity in complex situations: Separate symptoms from root causes, devise efficient debugging workflows, reproduce failures and drive lasting solutions that make the system more robust long term. When the root cause requires it, contribute directly to the layer that matters, drawing directly from the experts who develop core components of your system. Acceptance & Testing Automation: Define and run acceptance tests for platforms, payloads, and deployment configurations. Own readiness checks across calibration, software flashing, networking, sensors, and pre-mission setup. Make readiness measurable and repeatable. Field Deployment & End-User Interface: Install, configure, maintain, and support SE3 systems at test ranges, customer sites, partner demonstrations, exercises, and real-world deployments. Make sure our autonomous platforms perform reliably where it matters, enable end-users to succeed in their missions and represent SE3 with technical credibility outside the lab. Your Profile Most importantly, you’re structured, fast-moving, and mission-driven. You don’t wait for perfect information. You create clarity, iterate fast, and prefer finding and fixing root causes over applying patches. You hold a B.Sc., M.Sc. or similar degree in Robotics, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Embedded Systems, Mechatronics, or a related field. You bring multiple years of hands-on experience integrating, testing, operating, and troubleshooting complex robotic, UAV, embedded, automotive, industrial automation, or defence systems. You are proficient in using CAD software, creating wiring diagrams, building electromechanic prototypes and defining and executing test campaigns across hardware disciplines. You are familiar with soldering, crimping, using multimeters, oscilloscopes, serial consoles, or other lab and field equipment, with at least basic experience in command line, data analysis tools and Linux usage. You are proactive, hands-on and able to find effective solutions also under the constraints of field-campaigns and willing to travel and deploy across Europe.
